core_obligations: Assume M is finite and I-projective and choose a short exact sequence 0 to K to R^r to M to 0 (proof lines 17833-17835).
Dualise to obtain an injection of M dual into the double dual of R^r, which is R^r (proof lines 17835-17837).
Use that the class of the chosen extension is annihilated by I to factor multiplication by a on M through the map R^r to M (proof lines 17837-17840).
Dualise that factorisation to see that multiplication by a on M dual factors through the inclusion of M dual into R^r, and conclude that M dual is I-projective (proof lines 17840-17844).

difficulty_reason: The lemma is a closure property for the near-projective modules of the section: the dual of a finite I-projective module over a ring is again I-projective (statement lines 17826-17830). The proof is a 12-line argument (proof lines 17833-17844) which chooses a surjection from a finite free module onto M, dualises it to an injection of M dual into the free module, and then uses the description of I-projectivity through the Ext class of that surjection: since the class is annihilated by I, multiplication by a on M factors through the projection, and taking duals shows that multiplication by a on M dual factors through the inclusion of M dual into the free module, which is exactly I-projectivity of M dual. What has to be seen is the passage from the factorisation over M to the factorisation after dualising, and the choice of the presentation, both of which the author states in one sentence each.
